findings.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 — [P1, confidence 100, code `var maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024; // 10MB`] Replacing `max_${type}_size_kb` with one hard-coded admission limit breaks the configured per-type upload-policy contract, so lower site limits are bypassed in the client while higher configured limits become impossible to submit.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66 — [P1, confidence 100, code `while attempt > 0 && tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`] An arbitrary five-pass loop is used as the size-limit mechanism instead of enforcing the post-transform size invariant, so valid large images that still exceed the configured threshold after five 80% resizes are not automatically made uploadable despite this feature's contract.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:55 — [P2, confidence 75, code `FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, "discourse-upload-#{type}")`] The API URL ingestion path now owns a second, fixed 10 MB policy independent of `max_image_size_kb`, so deployments that intentionally permit a larger original image (and expect it to be transformed) are capped before the transformation pipeline can apply their configured policy.

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 — P2 (confidence 99; code `var maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024; // 10MB`; sibling user-config gates: `max_image_size_kb` and `max_attachment_size_kb`) — replacing the type-derived setting makes the upload acceptance and its “too large” notification disagree with both administrator-selected limits, so an attachment over `max_attachment_size_kb` or an image over a smaller `max_image_size_kb` is advertised as acceptable until a later rejection; rebuttal that 10 MB is the new image intake ceiling does not cover the `type === 'attachment'` path, and the finding survives the deletion/simplification test because retaining the existing type-indexed expression preserves the feature while preserving both user gates.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:55 — P2 (confidence 94; code `FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, "discourse-upload-#{type}")`; sibling user-config gates: `max_image_size_kb` controls the transformed result and `allow_animated_thumbnails` controls GIF conversion) — API URL uploads larger than 10 MB are discarded before the new downsize loop can transform them, so eligible large remote images cannot receive the promised automatic downsizing even when their eventual encoded size would satisfy `max_image_size_kb`; rebuttal that 10 MB is a deliberate intake cap is unsupported by the configured post-transform limit and survives the deletion/simplification test because using the existing configured limit (or an explicit separate intake gate) is required to make the feature apply consistently to this upload route.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:65 — P2 (confidence 91; code `attempt = 5` together with `OptimizedImage.downsize(..., "80%", allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails)`; sibling user-config gates: `max_image_size_kb > 0` enables resizing and `allow_animated_thumbnails` selects animated-image processing) — the fixed five 80%-dimension passes can leave a high-entropy image above a low configured byte cap, after which it is handed to `Upload.create_for` unmodified enough to violate the requested maximum rather than continuing or reporting that it cannot meet the limit; rebuttal that five passes is normally sufficient does not meet the setting’s arbitrary byte-limit contract, and the finding survives the deletion/simplification test because the fixed retry bound is the only behavior preventing the loop from satisfying its own `tempfile.size > max_image_size_kb` condition.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — P1 (confidence 100): `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails)` sends Rack 1.5 browser-upload tempfiles (created as `Tempfile.new("RackMultipart")`, so they have no image suffix) to ImageMagick with that extensionless path as the output, causing `convert` to have no output encoder/exit nonzero; because `convert_with` only returns false and the loop ignores it, every oversized browser image remains oversized and is subsequently rejected by `Upload.create_for` rather than being downsized.

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 — P1 confidence 75: replacing the configured limit with verbatim `var maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024; // 10MB` changes the requested automatic downsizing behavior into an unaccepted fixed 10-MB admission ceiling, so an administrator who permits images above 10 MB has those large images rejected in the browser rather than downsized to the configured allowed size.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — P1 confidence 100: `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails)` uses Rack browser-upload tempfiles with extensionless paths as ImageMagick output paths, so `convert` cannot select an output encoder and returns false (which the loop ignores), leaving every oversized browser image untransformed before `Upload.create_for` rejects it despite the asynchronous request having already returned success.

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 — P2 (confidence 100): `var maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024` replaces the type-specific configured limit for both images and attachments, so the image-only downsize feature also makes every attachment up to 10 MB pass client-side validation rather than respecting `max_attachment_size_kb`.

goldens.comment: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.

Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).

Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.
The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66 — [P1, confidence 100, code `while attempt > 0 && tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`] An arbitrary five-pass loop is used as the size-limit mechanism instead of enforcing the post-transform size invariant, so valid large images that still exceed the configured threshold after five 80% resizes are not automatically made uploadable despite this feature's contract.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the loop at line 66 runs at most 5 times with 80% reduction each pass. If an image is still too large after 5 passes, the code continues without error - the upload will then fail later at Upload.create_for due to size validation. This is a legitimate edge-case concern about the feature's design: the comment says 'allow users to upload large images that will be automatically reduced to allowed size' but this contract isn't guaranteed for all valid images. However, this is a design/scope concern rather than a bug - the code works as written, it just may not handle all edge cases the feature intends to cover.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that the download limit is hardcoded to 10.megabytes at line 55, while the subsequent downsizing logic (lines 63-69) uses SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb to determine the target size. If a deployment has max_image_size_kb set higher than 10MB (e.g., 15MB), the download would be capped at 10MB before the transformation pipeline can process it, preventing users from uploading images larger than 10MB even when the site setting allows it. This is a real behavioral inconsistency introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 — P2 (confidence 99; code `var maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024; // 10MB`; sibling user-config gates: `max_image_size_kb` and `max_attachment_size_kb`) — replacing the type-derived setting makes the upload acceptance and its “too large” notification disagree with both administrator-selected limits, so an attachment over `max_attachment_size_kb` or an image over a smaller `max_image_size_kb` is advertised as acceptable until a later rejection; rebuttal that 10 MB is the new image intake ceiling does not cover the `type === 'attachment'` path, and the finding survives the deletion/simplification test because retaining the existing type-indexed expression preserves the feature while preserving both user gates.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that line 182 replaces `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` with a hardcoded `10 * 1024` (10MB). This means the client-side validation no longer respects the administrator-configured `max_attachment_size_kb` or `max_image_size_kb` settings. The finding correctly identifies that: 1) For attachments, the 10MB hardcoded value will allow uploads that exceed the configured `max_attachment_size_kb`, leading to later server-side rejection. 2) For images where `max_image_size_kb` is set lower than 10MB, the client will accept files that may still be rejected. The server-side code in uploads_controller.rb only handles image downsizing, not attachments, so the attachment path is genuinely broken. This is a real behavioral defect where client-side validation disagrees with server-side limits.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a real inconsistency in the diff. The new downsize loop at lines 63-68 is designed to automatically reduce large images to fit within max_image_size_kb. However, the FileHelper.download call at line 55 has a hardcoded 10.megabytes limit that will reject/discard files larger than 10MB before they can reach the downsize loop. This means API URL uploads between 10MB and whatever size could be downsized to fit max_image_size_kb will fail, while direct file uploads (which go through the JavaScript validation also hardcoded to 10MB at line 182) have the same issue. The finding correctly notes this creates an inconsistency where the feature cannot work for remote images larger than 10MB even if they could be successfully downsized.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:65 — P2 (confidence 91; code `attempt = 5` together with `OptimizedImage.downsize(..., "80%", allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails)`; sibling user-config gates: `max_image_size_kb > 0` enables resizing and `allow_animated_thumbnails` selects animated-image processing) — the fixed five 80%-dimension passes can leave a high-entropy image above a low configured byte cap, after which it is handed to `Upload.create_for` unmodified enough to violate the requested maximum rather than continuing or reporting that it cannot meet the limit; rebuttal that five passes is normally sufficient does not meet the setting’s arbitrary byte-limit contract, and the finding survives the deletion/simplification test because the fixed retry bound is the only behavior preventing the loop from satisfying its own `tempfile.size > max_image_size_kb` condition.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a loop that attempts to downsize an image up to 5 times (attempt = 5, decrementing each iteration) to get it under max_image_size_kb. However, if after 5 passes the image is still larger than the configured limit, the code continues to Upload.create_for without any error handling or notification. This means a high-entropy image with a low configured byte cap could still exceed the limit after processing. The finding correctly identifies that the fixed retry bound creates a scenario where the loop's condition (tempfile.size > max_image_size_kb) may never be satisfied, yet the upload proceeds anyway, violating the configured maximum size constraint.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — P1 (confidence 100): `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails)` sends Rack 1.5 browser-upload tempfiles (created as `Tempfile.new("RackMultipart")`, so they have no image suffix) to ImageMagick with that extensionless path as the output, causing `convert` to have no output encoder/exit nonzero; because `convert_with` only returns false and the loop ignores it, every oversized browser image remains oversized and is subsequently rejected by `Upload.create_for` rather than being downsized.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real bug in the diff. Looking at the code: 1) In uploads_controller.rb:67, `OptimizedImage.downsize` is called with `tempfile.path` as both input and output. 2) The diff shows `downsize` calls `optimize` which builds instructions and calls `convert_with`. 3) `convert_with` runs ImageMagick's convert command and returns `false` if exitstatus != 0, but the loop in uploads_controller.rb doesn't check this return value (`while attempt > 0 && tempfile.size > ...`). 4) The finding correctly identifies that Rack tempfiles (created as `Tempfile.new('RackMultipart')`) don't have image extensions, which can cause ImageMagick to fail to determine the output format. 5) When convert fails, the loop continues decrementing attempts but the file remains unchanged, eventually exhausting attempts without actually downsizing. This is a legitimate bug where the downsize operation silently fails for browser uploads.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 — P1 confidence 75: replacing the configured limit with verbatim `var maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024; // 10MB` changes the requested automatic downsizing behavior into an unaccepted fixed 10-MB admission ceiling, so an administrator who permits images above 10 MB has those large images rejected in the browser rather than downsized to the configured allowed size.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that in the JavaScript file, the dynamic configuration `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` is replaced with a hardcoded `10 * 1024` (10MB). This means the client-side validation now uses a fixed 10MB limit regardless of what the administrator has configured. If an admin sets max_image_size_kb to something larger than 10MB, the browser will reject files over 10MB before they even reach the server where the downsizing logic exists. This is a real behavioral change that breaks the intended functionality for admins who want to allow larger uploads.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — P1 confidence 100: `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails)` uses Rack browser-upload tempfiles with extensionless paths as ImageMagick output paths, so `convert` cannot select an output encoder and returns false (which the loop ignores), leaving every oversized browser image untransformed before `Upload.create_for` rejects it despite the asynchronous request having already returned success.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real issue: the code calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)` where tempfile.path is a Rack tempfile path that typically lacks a file extension. Looking at the diff, the `downsize` method passes dimensions to `optimize`, which then passes them to instruction methods like `downsize_instructions` or `downsize_instructions_animated`. The animated check uses `from =~ /\.GIF$/i` which would fail on extensionless paths. More critically, ImageMagick's `convert` command relies on file extensions to determine output format - without an extension, it cannot determine the encoder. The loop checks nothing (no return value check on `downsize`), so if it fails, the loop continues but the file remains unchanged. The finding correctly identifies that this would leave oversized images untransformed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 — P2 (confidence 100): `var maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024` replaces the type-specific configured limit for both images and attachments, so the image-only downsize feature also makes every attachment up to 10 MB pass client-side validation rather than respecting `max_attachment_size_kb`.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that in utilities.js line 182, the code changes from `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` (which would use type-specific settings like max_image_size_kb or max_attachment_size_kb) to a hardcoded `10 * 1024` (10MB). This means both images AND attachments will now pass client-side validation up to 10MB, regardless of the configured max_attachment_size_kb setting. The server-side downsize feature (in uploads_controller.rb) only applies to images (`FileHelper.is_image?(filename)`), so attachments that exceed their configured limit will pass client validation but may fail server-side. This is a real behavioral bug where attachment size limits are no longer enforced on the client side.
